note: Hand-curated, sourced entries. Special election for the seat JD Vance vacated.

OH-senate.statusNote: Special election: former Sen. Sherrod Brown (D) faces appointed Sen. Jon Husted (R) for the seat JD Vance vacated.

OH-governor.statusNote: Open seat (Gov. DeWine term-limited): Vivek Ramaswamy (R) faces Dr. Amy Acton (D).

OH-house-9.statusNote: Rep. Marcy Kaptur (D), the longest-serving woman in congressional history, faces former state Rep. Derek Merrin (R) in a 2024 rematch in a Toledo-area district Trump carried by 11 points. Merrin won the May 5, 2026 GOP primary with 44.1%. We know who's running, positions not researched yet.

candidates.name: Sherrod Brown
candidates.background: U.S. Senator 1993–2025 (House then Senate); lost his seat in 2024, now running in the 2026 special election. Known as one of the Senate's most labor-focused members.

cost.label: Career centered on working-class economics: opposed NAFTA/CAFTA, paid-sick-days bills, Stop Predatory Investing Act (Wikipedia)

health.label: Voted for the ACA; backed Medicare buy-in at 55+; earlier co-sponsored Medicare for All (Wikipedia)

housing.label: Co-sponsored YIGBY housing act and Stop Predatory Investing Act limiting corporate home-buying (Wikipedia)

taxes.label: Fought the 2017 tax law as favoring the wealthy and corporations (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Pushed EPA to regulate PFAS 'forever chemicals' (Wikipedia)

immigration.label: Supports DACA legal status for DREAMers (2018) while backing 'resources for Border Patrol agents; expedite asylum process' (2024) (OnTheIssues)

education.label: 'Longtime opponent of vouchers for private schools'; cut student loan rates, raise Pell Grants, free community college (OnTheIssues)

safety.label: Backs police de-escalation training and cutting recidivism through Second Chance reentry programs (OnTheIssues)

repro.label: 'Restore Roe v. Wade abortion protection'; keep federal funding for family planning clinics (OnTheIssues)

democracy.label: Automatic voter registration for all citizens, expand early and mail voting; says photo-ID rules discourage voting (OnTheIssues)

candidates.name: Jon Husted
candidates.background: Appointed U.S. Senator (Jan 2025) after JD Vance became Vice President; previously Ohio Lt. Governor and Secretary of State. Running to keep the seat in the special election.

taxes.label: Deregulation record: InnovateOhio, office budget cuts, lower business fees (Wikipedia)

climate.label: Sponsored 2025 repeal of appliance energy-efficiency standards as regulatory burden (Wikipedia)

education.label: Backed charter schools and expanded access to private/religious education (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: 'Easy to vote and hard to cheat': voter-roll purges (upheld 5–4 in Husted v. Randolph Institute), uniform early-voting limits (Wikipedia)

health.label: Defends One Big Beautiful Bill Medicaid work requirements: 'work 20 hours a week or take classes' (Blue Water Healthy Living)

immigration.label: Backs deporting people 'who came here illegally and committed crimes' while wanting legal pathways for agriculture and construction workers (Blue Water Healthy Living)

repro.label: Campaign pledge: 'Jon will always stand for life, defend the most vulnerable' (Husted for Senate)

cost.label: Voted yes on S.J.Res. 18 to repeal the CFPB's $5 overdraft fee cap, March 27, 2025 (Senate roll call vote 153)

housing.label: Voted for ROAD to Housing Act provisions he framed as 'cut outdated red tape that drives up housing costs and unlock more private investment' with no taxpayer spending (Husted Senate press release)

safety.label: Voted yes on the HALT Fentanyl Act permanently placing fentanyl analogues on Schedule I, March 14, 2025 (Senate roll call vote 127)

candidates.name: Vivek Ramaswamy
candidates.background: Biotech entrepreneur, author, and 2024 presidential candidate; briefly co-led DOGE. Endorsed by the Ohio Republican Party for the open governor seat.

immigration.label: Advocates ending birthright citizenship; merit-based H-1B reform (Wikipedia)

climate.label: 'Burn coal,' frack without 'environmental agendas'; opposes EV subsidies (Wikipedia)

education.label: Pledged to abolish the U.S. Education Department; opposes CRT in schools (Wikipedia)

safety.label: Mixed: military action against cartels, but supports federal marijuana legalization (Wikipedia)

democracy.label: Proposed raising the voting age to 25 absent service or a civics test (2023 campaign) (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Plan: 'Slash red tape that drives up costs and stalls business growth' plus low-cost energy and lower taxes as the affordability fix (Vivek for Ohio)

taxes.label: 'Phase out the state income tax,' 'slash property taxes immediately,' and 'cut government bloat so our government lives within its means' (Vivek for Ohio)

repro.label: 'Unapologetically pro-life'; praised Iowa's six-week ban as 'progress that should come from the states'; open to a federal ban (Heartland Signal)

health.label: Calls Medicaid 'a vital program' while backing work requirements for those able to work; previously called Medicaid without work requirements 'a mistake' (Statehouse News Bureau)

nullNotes.housing: checked vivekforohio.com plan (homeownership mentioned only via lower cost of living, no housing policy) and Ballotpedia, nothing documented

candidates.name: Amy Acton
candidates.background: Physician and former Ohio Department of Health director, the state's trusted voice in the early COVID-19 response.

health.label: Campaign centers healthcare costs: Medicaid, caregiver tax credits, marketplace affordability (Wikipedia)

cost.label: Affordability agenda: 'crack down on price gouging,' a price-gouging hotline, Ohio Rx drug-purchasing platform, wage-theft enforcement (Acton for Governor)

climate.label: Lower bills by 'incorporating the lowest-cost and cleanest sources of energy'; regulators 'not beholden to utility companies' (Acton for Governor)

education.label: 'Public money should be for public schools': restore constitutional funding, reform the 'corrupt school voucher system' (Acton for Governor)

safety.label: Mixed: 'fully fund the police and public safety' alongside investing in 'addiction treatment, mental health services and community programming' (Acton for Governor)

repro.label: Protect 'safe, legal abortion care, contraception, fertility treatments, and miscarriage care,' free from government interference (Acton for Governor)

democracy.label: Will 'help try again to pass a redistricting reform amendment in 2027'; called GOP ballot language 'lawless' (Signal Akron)

immigration.label: Mixed: 'if people are here illegally, we need to enforce the laws' but insists ICE act 'lawfully' and says Ohioans are 'horrified' by enforcement actions (Ideastream Public Media)

candidates.now: Former Director, Ohio Department of Health

candidates.name: Marcy Kaptur
candidates.background: Marcy Kaptur has represented Ohio's Toledo-based 9th District since 1983 and is the longest-serving woman in congressional history. A former urban planner and Carter administration urban policy adviser, she narrowly defeated Derek Merrin in 2024 and was unopposed in the 2026 Democratic primary.

candidates.name: Derek Merrin
candidates.background: Derek Merrin is a former Ohio state representative (2016-2025) who earlier served as mayor and councilman of Waterville and worked as a realtor and business owner. The 2024 GOP nominee who narrowly lost to Kaptur, he won the May 5, 2026 primary with 44.1% over Josh Williams and three others.
